correctness.rationale: The real Hilbert–Schmidt energy identity forces any imaginary-axis eigenoperator to commute with all even-site projectors. Such operators are parity-block diagonal; the Hamiltonian commutator is off-block, eliminating nonzero imaginary frequencies. Write H with off-diagonal block B. The even diagonal entries of a fixed operator agree wherever BB* has a nonzero entry. For each diagonal step the two length-two paths have the same flat phase, and these steps connect the even sublattice, so the even block is scalar. The odd block is then scalar on im B* and arbitrary on ker B. The adjoint has the same kernel, and Hilbert–Schmidt contractivity excludes a peripheral Jordan block; orthogonal projection onto the resulting algebra gives the trace-preserving limit. For the count, the two opposite-cosine branches on the momentum torus are cosets of kernels of (i,j)↦ni±mj mod mn, each of size g if solvable. Intersection forces both twists zero and consists of two momenta. Equal even/odd sizes give rank-nullity k=dim ker H/2. Independent exact phase matching corroborated 1,152 rational-twist cases. Odd parity-preserving translations fix the dark projection's diagonal (no symmetry of the numerical rates is required); its common odd value is 2k/N. This gives the stated finite return and rescaled square limits, including the different k but equal rescaled limit at the two crossings.
residual_risks: The input checker was inspected, not executed. Finite rational grids do not test all exact flux resonances; the proof does.
The conclusion is for flat hopping phases, positive individual even-site rates, and time taken to infinity before size. No uniform relaxation rate follows.
